body:
## Problem

A summary selector inside an inline function can forward an omitted ordinary
formal argument to an `across()` function. Ordinary R preserves whether that
argument is missing, including the distinction between an omitted formal with
and without a default.

```r
data <- data.frame(x = 1:3)
f <- function(x, extra = 10) if (missing(extra)) 100 else 300
expression <- rlang::expr((function(a, ...) dplyr::across(..., extra = a))(
  .cols = x, .fns = f
))
suppressWarnings(dplyr::summarise(data, value = !!expression))$value$x
# 100
suppressWarnings(summarize_with_margins(data, value = !!expression))$value$x
# Current main: error. PR #1149: 300.
```

On main `a563444f831d793c08c15e94510ff09e3377c300`, R 4.6.1, dplyr 1.2.1,
rlang 1.3.0 and tidyselect 1.2.1 on aarch64 macOS, the Margin verb raises
`... must be empty` before reaching `f`. At PR #1149's `0df69707`, the same
call returns 300. The ordinary dplyr result is 100. Main was reproduced from
a disposable source archive; no relevant tests were skipped.

This is distinct from #1138's populated selector forwarding and #1151's
unnamed top-level `across()` expansion. The forwarded `a` is a separately
written function formal, not a missing member of the helper's forwarded dots.
An omitted formal with a default must be tested separately: base R reports
`missing(a)` as true in its own function but passes its default as a supplied
argument to a nested function. Therefore checking `missing(a)` alone is not
sufficient to decide the nested argument's missingness.

All-state issue and PR searches for `"missing" "forward"` did not find a
matching report; the relevant PR #1149 was reviewed as described above.
title: [P2] Preserve missing formal arguments forwarded into inline selectors
